newsitem.title: USA: Travelers Smith Barney Q4 rises.
newsitem.headline: Travelers Smith Barney Q4 rises.

text.p: Travelers Group Inc said its Smith Barney investment bank achieved operating earnings of $226.4 million in the fourth quarter, up 21 percent from $186.9 million in the year ago period.
For the full year, Smith Barney reported operating earnings of $888.8 million, up 48 percent from $599.5 million in 1995.
Travelers/Aetna Property Casualty Corp reported fourth quarter operating earnings of $214.5 million, up 98 percent from a year ago. Travelers has an 82 percent stake in Travelers/Aetna.
For the full year, Travelers/Aetna reported operating earnings of $691.5 million, up 68 percent.
The Travelers/Aetna earnings reflect the acquisition of Aetna Inc's property-casualty operations in April 1996.
Travelers said its consumer finance operation reported fourth quarter operating earnings of $52.3 million, down 19 percent from $64.9 million a year ago.
The consumer finance business reported 1996 operating earnings of $222.4 million, down 10 percent from $246.4 million in 1995.
Travelers said Commercial Credit's results were hurt by higher loan losses, reflecting record levels of personal bankruptcies industrywide.
"We still expect improvement in this segment in the second half of 1997, however, which should make year-over-year, 1997 to 1996 comparisons favorable," Travelers chief executive Sanford Weill said.
Weill said he believes the 1997 outlook for Travelers is positive.

"The outlook for 1997 is very positive. Our businesses are in excellent operating shape, cross-selling ventures among our companies are flourishing, and the bulk of our earnings comes from predictable, recurring sources," he said.
"We believe Travelers Group is well positioned for continued growth and profitability. As we start our second decade, we are confident that the best is yet to come," he said.
